A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, methods, and main experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including v2's additional appendix material and checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original functional subgraph detection and fuzzy boundary identification experiments, component ablations, and encoder comparisons in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds larger-circuit evaluations and a VF3 comparison in Appendix B, Tables 7–9.

M1.justification: Both versions use DeepGate2 and DeepCell encoders, classification with intra-modal and inter-modal InfoNCE alignment, and subsequent node-segmentation fine-tuning. The added invariance discussion and background explain the existing procedure without changing its components or objectives.

E1.justification: The three source datasets and two tasks are retained. Appendix B.3 adds a larger-circuit population from ForgeEDA, spanning 100–10,000 nodes, extending circuit-scale coverage within the existing domain.

E2.justification: v2 newly evaluates the structural matcher VF3 against the proposed method in Table 9; v1's VF2 usage was preprocessing verification, not a reported performance baseline. Original neural comparisons remain. The new larger-circuit evaluation excludes ABGNN results because of reported memory failure.

E3.justification: Appendix B.4 introduces a comparison restricted to ForgeEDA circuits with fewer than 50 nodes and reports runtime alongside predictive metrics. These are additional evaluation settings; the original splits, preprocessing, training budgets, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3 adds a targeted scalability analysis documenting detection performance on larger circuits and ABGNN's out-of-memory failure. The existing alignment, pretraining, segmentation, and encoder-substitution analyses are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify mean ± standard deviation over three independent runs for Tables 1–2. v2's new checklist additionally describes these as '1-sigma' standard-error bars, creating an inconsistent reporting statement. No increased run count or changed uncertainty computation is established.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–5 retain their scores, but substantial new results characterize additional settings. Tables 7–8 report larger-circuit F1 scores of 81.2±0.8% for Gsyn and 78.3±1.3% for Gpm. Table 9 reports VF3 precision of 100%, recall of 0.32%, and F1 of 0.65%, versus the proposed method's 90.2% F1 on the small-circuit Gsyn task; reported runtimes are 480.8 versus 8.0 seconds. These are new evaluations, not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Section 2.3 and Proposition 4 extend functional-equivalence preservation from replacement of the query to replacement of the candidate graph, with an added proof paragraph in Appendix A. Other definitions, assumptions, and proofs are retained. Appendix D's InfoNCE formula explains an existing loss.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same conceptual contributions, two-stage framework, and headline results of 93.8% detection accuracy and 91.3% DICE. The additional experiments do not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly connects equivalence preservation to alignment, interprets the larger-circuit results as a scalability challenge, and explains VF3's low recall through synthesis-induced structural changes. Section 5's limitations remain unchanged. The new scalability paragraph's stated 95.3%-to-81.2% F1 decline incorrectly pairs Gpm and Gsyn results.

D1.justification: v2 adds a repository link in the abstract and states in its checklist that code and data accompany the supplemental material. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, training-time information, and sampling algorithm are retained. The PDFs establish added access information, not the repository's contents or accessibility.

R1.justification: v2 adds the VF3 reference and discusses its relationship to functional subgraph matching through an evaluated comparison. The broader literature positioning is retained; changes to the ForgeEDA reference are bibliographic reformatting.

P1.justification: v2 adds background explanations in Appendix D, a short alignment rationale, experimental subsections, an acknowledgment, and a NeurIPS checklist. It also makes small wording corrections and updates the conference footer. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6–9 for the larger-circuit statistics, detection results, and VF3 comparison; the original dataset table becomes Table 10. Existing tables and Algorithm 1 are repositioned through reflow, while Figures 1–3 and the established table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: The larger-circuit tests turn a previously discussed scalability concern into concrete evidence, and the VF3 comparison strengthens the empirical distinction between structural and functional matching. Background explanations and a repository pointer also help readers. These gains outweigh localized reporting problems, but the mixed-task F1 comparison, inconsistent checklist uncertainty description, and malformed sentence in the added proof limit the improvement.
